title: Odile and the Cover
premise: Ulyana Nystrom, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent six years buried in a witness-protection identity, attributing disasters no airline wants to own. When the safe house appears on a real-estate site with interior photos — including her daughter's drawing still taped to the fridge — she realizes the network that trained her, Meridian, is flushing its assets before a Frankfurt market opening that will launder their liability into clean capital. Hunting the broker who listed the house, Ulyana falls for Elias Varga, the ex-Meridian archivist sent to erase her, and must choose between the duty that kept her alive and the justice row twelve never got. In the end she burns Meridian's ledger live to the Frankfurt exchanges at market open, trades her invisibility for a public name, and lets Elias walk away carrying the only copy of her family's true final report.
about_author: Paloma Villalobos is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading black-box transcripts before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse in northern Portugal, where she keeps a wall of unattributed accident reports.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Opening on an anonymous crash-site inspection in rural Norway, Ulyana files yet another report stamped 'pilot error' while privately cataloguing what really happened. A flashback to row twelve establishes her grief and her deal with the protection program. Emotional beat: controlled numbness cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Her handler sends a routine link: the safe house is for sale, photos included — her kitchen, her daughter's drawing, the scratch on the doorframe marking heights. She confirms the listing traces to a shell company she recognizes from old case files: Meridian. Emotional beat: cold horror hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Handler Down
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, intercut with a brief handler POV. She drives through the night to confront her protection officer and finds his office cleared, his phone forwarding to a number in Zurich. The program that hid her is being dismantled from inside. Emotional beat: betrayal; the floor dropping out.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Elias's POV introduced. Sent by Meridian to 'close out' Ulyana's file, Elias instead watches her from across a Copenhagen hotel bar and hesitates — he recognizes her name from the ledger he was ordered to shred years ago. He approaches not as a hunter but as a defector-in-waiting. Emotional beat: dangerous curiosity.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Elias shows Ulyana the archive: every attributed disaster, including Flight 4471, priced and sold. They form an uneasy alliance — she needs the ledger, he needs absolution. First trust, first touch. Emotional beat: love kindling against explicit duty.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Elias recovers the sealed 4471 transcript Meridian buried: the crew fought a known defect, and someone chose the cheaper fix. Ulyana finally hears her family's last minutes. Grief becomes fuel. Emotional beat: devastation transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Countdown
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With 72 hours until market open, they map Meridian's laundering structure — the IPO that converts blood into shareholder value. Meridian's cleaners close in; a safe contact turns them in. Emotional beat: ticking-clock dread, intimacy sharpened by mortality.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Captured briefly by his former team, Elias is offered reinstatement if he delivers Ulyana. He burns his own cover instead, feeding Ulyana the exchange-floor access codes. Emotional beat: duty fully inverted; love chosen at cost.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. From a rented flat above the Frankfurt exchange, Ulyana pushes the full ledger — transcripts, memos, signatures — into every terminal as the bell rings. Meridian's valuation collapses mid-trade. Cleaners breach the stairwell; Elias covers her exit and vanishes into the crowd. Emotional beat: catharsis amid chaos.

chapters.title: Attributed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Months later, hearings underway and her real name public for the first time, Ulyana visits the 4471 memorial and adds row twelve's truth to the record. A postcard arrives, unsigned, with a single word: 'safe.' Emotional beat: mourning resolved into memory; justice outside the law, love surviving absence.
